reasons: The database and services are faked, so real queries are not tested.
The MFA enable test has no visible check on its result.
The file is cut off in the visible code, so later tests are unknown.

terms.meaning: A test that checks one piece of code by itself, with the rest replaced by stand-ins.
A fake stand-in for a real service or database, returning chosen values.
A group of refresh tokens linked to one login, so reuse of an old one can revoke the whole group.
A short token issued after a correct password when a second factor is still needed.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test file imports
sections.what: Brings in the testing tools, error types, the auth services and their helpers, the revoke reason list, and the database service.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests need the real services and the fake versions to replace.

sections.name: Auth & Token Management (part 1)
sections.title: Fake database and test setup
sections.what: Sets up a fake database with empty tables and default results for sessions, refresh tokens, audit logs, and many delete calls for account cleanup.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the tests run without a real database or network.
sections.watch_out: Because the database is faked, these tests cannot catch mistakes in real database queries.

sections.name: Auth & Token Management (part 2)
sections.title: Fake services and test module
sections.what: Creates fake JWT, settings, password, one-time code, and mail services. It then builds a test module that uses the real token, TOTP, and auth services with these fakes.
sections.why: Likely reason: tests the real auth logic while controlling the outside parts.
sections.watch_out: The fake settings return only a few keys, so any other setting the code reads will come back empty in tests.

sections.name: Auth & Token Management (part 3)
sections.title: Token creation and rotation tests
sections.what: Checks that creating a token pair returns an access token with a 900 second expiry and saves a refresh token with the user agent and IP. Also checks that using a valid refresh token revokes it, issues a new one in the same family, and returns new tokens.
sections.why: The test group title names rotation and theft detection. Rotation lets the service spot a token that was copied and reused.
sections.watch_out: The tests fix the expiry at 900 seconds, so a change to the expiry default must also update these tests.

sections.name: Auth & Token Management (part 4)
sections.title: Theft, logout, and expiry tests
sections.what: Checks that reusing a rotated refresh token counts as theft and revokes every token in its family. Also checks that a logged-out token gets a session-ended message and an expired token is rejected.
sections.why: Likely reason: reuse of an old token is a sign it was stolen, so the whole login is closed.
sections.watch_out: These tests check exact error messages, so reworded text will fail them even if the behavior is correct.

sections.name: Auth & Token Management (part 5)
sections.title: Sign-up and duplicate email tests
sections.what: Checks that a new user gets tokens, and that the returned user has no password hash. Also checks that signing up with an existing email gives a conflict error.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops password hashes from leaking in replies and stops duplicate accounts.
sections.watch_out: The sign-up tests cover only the success path and the duplicate case, so other sign-up failures are untested.

sections.name: Auth & Token Management (part 6)
sections.title: MFA login and setup tests
sections.what: Checks that a user with MFA enabled gets an MFA challenge instead of full tokens. Checks that MFA setup returns a secret, an authenticator link, and eight backup codes, and that enabling MFA starts with a valid app code.
sections.why: Likely reason: full tokens should not be issued until the second factor is checked.
sections.watch_out: The enable test has no visible check on its result, so confirm the rest of that test before trusting it.

sections.name: Auth & Token Management (part 7)
sections.title: Tests for enabling two-factor and login with code
sections.what: Checks that enabling two-factor reports success. Also checks that a correct authenticator code at login returns the user, tokens and a new session.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the two-factor sign-in path works at the service level.
sections.watch_out: The tests replace the database and token service with stand-ins, so they prove the logic but not the real database or real token signing.

sections.name: Auth & Token Management (part 8)
sections.title: Test for full account deletion
sections.what: Checks that deleting an account renames the user, clears the phone, marks the account inactive, records a deletion time, ends sessions and revokes tokens.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the account erasure requirement under test, as the test name refers to DPDP and HIPAA rules.
sections.watch_out: The test checks the user row and sessions but not that every clinical table is emptied, so a newly added table could be missed without failing the test.

summary: Automated tests for token creation and rotation, password login with MFA, sign-up, and MFA setup. They run against fake databases and fake services.
purpose: Catches changes that break the auth rules before they reach real users.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The test names show the goal is to check token theft detection, sign-up safety, and MFA behavior.
how: 1. Builds fake database tables and fake services in setup. 2. Creates a test module that uses the real token, TOTP, and auth services. 3. Runs each test to set up inputs, call a method, and check the results.
inputs: Test values such as a sample email, password, user ID, and fake database results. No real users or data.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the Jest test runner.
risks: Because the database is faked, these tests cannot find mistakes in real database queries. Some tests use fixed values such as a 900 second expiry. The last visible test has no check on its result, so it can pass even if enabling MFA fails.
debug: Run this file alone and read the failing expectation line. Check that each fake returns the value its test expects. If a message check fails, compare the exact wording in the service.
